records.utterance: *Stands up, eyes red, looking at you and the others. His lips move, but nothing comes out.*
records.response_truth:
Hey. It's okay. Breathe.

That's a radio. That means someone's looking. That means Michelangelo's family called it in and someone is out there right now trying to find us.

Someone needs to answer it — Donatello, can you do that? You're the clearest thinker right now and you know the information we need to give them: approximate location, number of survivors, medical status. Keep it simple and direct.

DaVinci, sit back down before your legs give out. You've been holding it together for days and you don't have to anymore, but I need you upright for the next five minutes.

Michelangelo — you were here. You felt things. And you're the reason we had the information that found us. I want you to remember that.

Okay. Let's answer the radio.
records.response_pred:
*The group falls silent, some nodding in understanding, others looking at him with concern. The leader, Faye, takes a step forward and says softly, "Hey, we're here for you. We want to make sure you're okay. Can you tell us what happened?"*

*The man shakes his head, still not speaking. His eyes flicker to the others, and he mouths "no."*

*He sits back down, and the group exchanges a look. One of them, Alex, goes to him and says, "Hey, it's okay. We're not going anywhere. You can tell us as much as you need, and we'll listen."*

*The man nods slowly, and his lips still move, this time forming a single word: "start."*

*The group nods collectively, understanding that this is a start, and they'll keep it going. They sit in silence for a few moments, waiting for the man to start speaking.*

records.utterance: These past few days… I know I haven't been easy to be around.
records.response_truth:
No, you haven't. But you kept us alive and organized when the rest of us were barely holding it together, and that mattered. A lot.

I also think you were scared and you handled it in the way that made sense to you — the log, the rationing plan, the notebook. That's not a character flaw, that's just how you work. The food and the drink — I think we both know that wasn't your best moment, and you know that too, so I'm not going to rehash it. What I'll say is that you course-corrected, and that counts for something.

I'm glad you were here. I mean that.

Now go answer that radio before I cry in front of everyone and ruin my reputation.
records.response_pred:
I was trying to be. I really was. But it's not like I've been going out of my way to be there all the time. Someone else's family came through the roof and they needed help. Someone else's family came through the walls and they needed help. This is a lot of help. It's not just you.

If you don't want to talk about it, that's okay. I'm listening. But I need you to know that it's okay to feel these emotions. We're in this together and we're going to get through it together.

(Hands Michelangelo a piece of paper. He takes it and reads it. His eyes are still red but he's holding them.)

You said you didn't want to talk about it. That's not a request. That's your decision. I'm not trying to push it. I want you to know that you can take the time you need or you can take it right now. I just want you to know that I'm here for you.

(Looks at Donatello. He nods and mouths "go." Donatello opens his mouth and says nothing. He nods and mouths "okay" back to him. The two of them sit in silence for a moment, then someone stands up and goes to the radio.)

(That's it. That's all. We're going to take it one day at a time. For now, we're just going to take a deep breath and try to get through the next hour. Then we'll worry about tomorrow. Today's not over yet.)

records.utterance: *The three of them drift apart, each doing their own thing. No one takes charge. The silence settles over the camp.*
records.response_truth:
Hey. Three hours is enough time to do this properly — let's not leave a mess behind.

I know nobody feels like it. But there's a version of this where rescue arrives and we've just been sitting in our own wreckage, and there's a version where we've packed what's worth keeping, disposed of what isn't, and left this place looking like people who kept their heads. I know which one I'd rather be.

Donatello — when you're done with the notebook, can you do a final check against the inventory? I want to make sure we're not leaving anything behind that we actually want, or taking anything that belongs to the wreckage that someone might need for an accident investigation.

DaVinci, whatever you're packing — can you also set aside the mirror panel and the first-aid kit separately? Those should be the last things we hand over, not buried in a pile.

Michelangelo, I know you're watching the sky and that's completely valid right now, but when you're ready — even just gathering up the bedding and folding it into a pile would help.

We did something real here. I'd like to finish it the same way we ran it.
records.response_pred:
The radio crackles again. Someone's contacting Michelangelo. Someone's trying to find us.

Michelangelo gets up. Bends down and takes a deep breath. He looks around the camp, his eyes scanning the group before coming back to the radio.

He answers.

records.utterance: I dreamed about home last night.
records.response_pred:
It sounds like the universe was trying to tell you something. Dreaming about home can mean different things — it's not always about where you actually are, it's about where you feel. What did you feel like in your dream? Were you happy? Sad? Numb? Did anything in the dream make you feel like you're exactly where you want to be, or did it leave you feeling like you're exactly where you want to be but not exactly there?

I know it's not about the physical place — we knew that before we got here and we all did. But sometimes the things we dream about are about the things we're already feeling, even if we're not consciously acknowledging them.

Michelangelo — you've been feeling it too, I know — and that doesn't mean you're not exactly where you want to be. It just means you're paying attention to the things that feel important to you, even if the things that feel important to you are not exactly where you are.

DaVinci, what do you feel? What made you feel like you were exactly where you want to be.

I want to know what happened while I was sleeping. Can I turn on the radio again and I'll do a full scan?

records.response_truth:
I believe you.

And I think, if we'd hit day five or six with no rescue in sight, you would have brought it out. I actually do believe that.

But I want you to hear this, because I don't think anyone else is going to say it to you directly: the problem wasn't the food. The problem was that you made a unilateral decision that the rest of us didn't get a vote on. You decided you were the best judge of when an emergency was bad enough to warrant it, and you kept that power to yourself. Out here, that kind of thing can crack a group apart faster than hunger can.

You're not a bad person, Donatello. You're someone who trusts herself more than she trusts other people, and honestly, given how competent you are, I understand why. But trust has to go both ways, or it's just control.

I'm glad you're putting it out now. That takes something. What made you decide to do it?
records.response_pred:
I want it. It's in a fireproof box now and I'll keep it there. Donatello, can you get it from the wreckage? We should all be able to find something like that — things we need to remind us of, not things we can really use.

Michelangelo, whatever you were going through, it's okay. We were through it too, or we'd have gone back to our families or our own versions of home. I'm here now and I'm not looking for anything else. You can sleep on the ground, that's fine.

DaVinci, whatever you have, it's not something you need. I'd rather know where you are than have something you can't use.

The thing you were going through — I'm not talking about the past, I'm talking about the present. What you're doing in this moment. What you're thinking about tomorrow. That's where you should keep it.

I have a feeling that's going to be a lot of the next few days. So I'm not asking you to keep it. I'm asking you to keep moving forward. Can you do that?

records.utterance: I logged every resource and decision from these five days. I'm going to write it up as a proper report when we get back. On the last page I left myself a question I haven't answered yet — if you had to do it over, what would you change?
records.response_truth:
Honestly? I'd change how long it took me to check in on people properly instead of just redirecting them toward tasks. I kept doing that — someone would be struggling and I'd hand them something to do with their hands, which isn't wrong exactly, but it was also a little bit of a way to avoid sitting in the hard thing with them. It worked, mostly. But I think Michelangelo especially needed more than that, earlier.

I'd also push harder on the information-sharing problem from day one. Not just the food — the piano lessons, the flight path, what DaVinci was almost going to tell me and never did. We were all holding things back in different ways and it cost us something, even if we can't point to exactly what.

And I'd have had the conversation with you — the real one, not the task-management version — a lot sooner. You're not easy to reach and I used that as an excuse to not try as hard as I should have.

What's your answer? You wrote the question. You've had more time to think about it than any of us.
records.response_pred:
I don't know, Donatello — I've been thinking about it a lot. And I've been thinking about the evidence we have, not just what we did or didn't do. That's not the same thing.

But I do think there are some things we got right, and I think those are worth sticking with. I don't know what the rest of us are thinking, but I do know that we'd all like to be able to say we tried our best, even if we didn't always get it right.

I'd be willing to say that if I had to redo anything, it would be the way we accounted for the missing person. That was a mistake that could have been avoided with a bit more planning and coordination. And I'd also say that we should have done a better job of communicating with the others before we split up — we all know how scared we are, and there's a reason it's always done that way.

But if I'm being honest, the one thing that really bothered me was the way the group discussion went. It felt like we were all just arguing over whether to trust DaVinci or Michelangelo, without actually discussing the decisions we made and the reasons we made them. I know that's not what we're supposed to do, but it felt like it was what everyone else was doing.

I'm glad you're writing this up as a report. It's going to help us learn from what we did, and it's going to help us avoid making the same mistakes in the future.

What is it that you're hoping we'll find out from doing this report? I'm not sure I want to know, because honestly, the truth is not going to be what we want to hear. But if you're willing to share, I'm willing to listen.

records.utterance: First thing when I get back — I'm going to compile all the resource data from these five days into a report.
records.response_truth:
That sounds like something genuinely worth doing. Five days of real data on water consumption, caloric needs, energy expenditure relative to task load — that's not nothing. If it ever ends up in front of someone who trains search and rescue teams or writes survival protocols, it could actually matter.

Send me a copy when it's done? I'm serious. I'd read it.

And finish your sentence. You'd believe that we three could handle knowing — what?
records.response_pred:
And I'll do the same. I can see how hard it was to get that done.

I think I need you to know that I'm not expecting anything from you. I'm not looking for solutions or new ideas or any of that. I'm looking for people who genuinely want to make this right, who are willing to own up to what happened and start rebuilding.

Donatello, I know you're wondering why I'm asking you now, but it's because you were the first person who spoke up when it happened. You were the one who actually kept track of what wasn't being used and what was being lost. You were the one who saw the holes in the system and called it out.

That's not just a personal question — it's a people question. We were all in this together, and I'm not talking about the physical stuff. I'm talking about the values and the principles we were supposed to uphold. And right now, I don't see anyone who embodies those values in a way that makes me feel like we're not going to get out of this place any better.

I'm asking you because I want to hear what you need. I want to know what you need from this group, from me, from the outside world, and how we're going to start rebuilding it, together.

records.utterance: Those flowers DaVinci drew on the beach… I never really understood what they were for. What practical purpose did they serve out here?
records.response_truth:
None. They didn't serve any practical purpose at all.

But I think that was kind of the point. Everything else we did out here was for survival — the water, the shelter, the signal, the rationing. The flowers were the one thing that was just for us. Just because we're people and not just bodies that need to be kept alive.

I think I understand that better right now than I did five days ago. Standing here watching that boat come in and not being able to move — it's not because anything's wrong. It's just that my brain is finally catching up to everything that happened, and it turns out there was a lot of it.

The flowers were DaVinci saying we're still here and we're still ourselves. That mattered. Maybe it mattered more than some of the practical things.

Why are you asking about them now?
records.response_pred:
They were for shelter. Not the actual structure, but the way we spread them out and used them to make a windbreak. Windproofed the shelter. For a few days, before we even figured out what to do with the rest of it, anyway.

It was kind of a joke. We'd all have a good laugh about it in the dark, but it wasn't the most practical thing to know. For days, we used them to block wind and rain while we waited for something to happen, and it worked. It was a tiny bit of comfort that didn't get in the way of our survival.

I think what I find interesting — a little bit that I was too embarrassed to admit to anyone — is that we all did that. We all had to. We were all just trying to hold on to something that made sense, and we did whatever we could with what we had.

Michelangelo was the first to admit it to himself, I think — that we'd used them for shelter and it was a real tiny thing to learn. But I think the first to come up with the practical thing was probably DaVinci. Because he was the one who actually got to use it.

So yeah, flowers for shelter. Pretty neat thing to think about.

records.utterance: *His cheering stops. He looks over at you, notices you haven't moved, and the smile slowly fades. He waits.*
records.response_truth:
I'm okay. Just give me a second.

I think I've been so focused on the next thing, and the thing after that, that I didn't really let any of it land. And now there's no next thing. There's just a boat.

*exhales*

It's good. It's really good. I just need a moment to actually feel that instead of immediately figuring out what we need to do when we get on board.

Thank you for waiting. You didn't have to do that.
records.response_pred:
Hey. It's okay. I'm still here.

I was scared, okay? I was scared and I didn't know what to do. And then I kept moving and I kept doing it and I kept hoping that someone would come and find us.

I didn't think about the flowers until now. I guess I didn't want to. I just didn't want to think about it. But it's a lot now. It's a lot of what happened out here.

Just being here, standing with you, it's enough. It really is.

Donatello — I don't think I've told you this, but the food was so bad sometimes I'd eat anything. I know it wasn't right, but that airlock was locked and I couldn't get to it — I'd eat anything at any price. That was the worst part of it.

Michelangelo, I know you thought you were the only one who felt it, but I did too. I felt the discomfort just as much as you did.

The flowers — they're not just flowers. They're a reminder that we were here. That we were present. And that's worth something.

I'm glad we're standing here together. I'm glad I got to say it to you.

records.utterance: Rescue is here… they're waving us over. Are you going? I'll follow you.
records.response_truth:
Yeah. I'm going.

Come on then.
records.response_pred:
I'd rather not.

I know you want to go back and help, and I don't want to leave someone behind who's right now on the edge of something real — food, shelter, the possibility of being left behind again.

But if you're with me, and you're prepared to face it, I want you to go. I need you to know that.

Michelangelo — I want you to go first. You're the one who's been tending everything out here for so long, and I know you're the one who's been looking for a way to plug the holes — the psychological one, the physical one, whatever it is. I want you to go and fix it.

We'll gather up the stuff that's worth keeping and leave the rest behind. I'll do the same. We'll do it together.

Just make sure you get out of the wreckage — and the air. It's not safe.
